- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.4), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Overshoots after sharp spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days) are common; cap forecast at 10-15% above peak for next 5 days.
- Model often overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3-5 day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast.
- If last 3-5 days show strong upward momentum + sentiment > 0.6, forecast should not exceed 10% above recent high unless confirmed by technicals.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.0–0.4), model tends to lag; forecast should be 1-2 days ahead of true price, but not more than 5% above recent mean.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above 30-day average, reduce by 1-2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid sharp upward revisions if sentiment is weak or declining; prefer gradual, sentiment-aligned drift.
